title: Web console epic P2: chat UI panel — streaming render of orchestrator output + subagent/tool activity
description:
EPIC "Agentic OS web console" — P2 front-end chat. Add a chat panel to the board server's served HTML (inline assets, zero-dep, simple HTML — nothing for the user to install) that consumes the TASK-051 streaming endpoint and renders a live conversation with the orchestrator.

Deliverables:
1. A chat panel in the page: scrollable message history (user turns + orchestrator turns), an input box + send button, and a busy/streaming indicator. On send it POSTs to /api/chat/:sessionId and renders the streamed normalized events from GET /api/chat/:sessionId/stream incrementally (text deltas appended live).
2. Surface the AGENTIC activity that makes this feel like an OS, not a chatbot: when the stream reports a tool_use or a subagent (developer/reviewer/researcher) spawn, show a compact activity chip/line (e.g. "▸ spawned developer", "▸ moved TASK-xxx → in_review") distinct from plain assistant text. Errors render as a clear inline error, not a silent stall.
3. A session id is established per tab (per the TASK-051 design) and reused for the tab's lifetime so continuity holds. Reconnect/stream-end handled gracefully (no infinite spinner).
4. XSS discipline matching the existing board/graph code: build DOM via createElement + textContent, NEVER innerHTML with stream content. Orchestrator/user text is untrusted display data.

Front-end behavior over a real browser → verification_tier tests-after with a UAT step (human-observable). Add a MINIMAL set of regression locks only where pure logic exists (e.g. the client event-to-DOM mapping helper if factored out, or any normalization shared with the server); do not over-spec DOM rendering. The board HTML is inside src/task-board.js which is bundled → rebuild dist/ and run test:all at hand-off (TASK-049 gate). Provide a terse UAT script (open console, type a message, observe streamed reply + an activity chip when a subagent spawns, observe a clean error path).
acceptance_criteria: The served page includes a chat panel (message history, input + send, streaming indicator) that POSTs a turn to /api/chat/:sessionId and renders streamed normalized events incrementally (orchestrator text appears token/delta-wise, not only after the full turn).

tool_use and subagent-spawn events render as distinct compact activity chips/lines (visually separable from plain assistant text), and a stream error renders as a clear inline error rather than a silent stall or infinite spinner.
A per-tab session id is established and reused for the tab lifetime (continuity preserved across multiple turns in the same tab); stream end / reconnect is handled without a stuck busy indicator.
All stream/user content is rendered via createElement + textContent (no innerHTML with untrusted content), consistent with the existing board/graph XSS discipline.
Any extracted pure-logic helper (e.g. event→view mapping) carries a minimal regression lock; no redundant DOM-render specs are added (new-test budget respected).

dist/ rebuilt and npm run test:all green at hand-off; a terse UAT script is recorded on the ticket and run with the human (send a message → streamed reply; trigger a subagent → activity chip; error path → inline error), all steps PASS.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: Plan + tier: verification_tier=tests-after → single IMPL phase, then minimal regression locks, then UAT (human-observable). Touches the bundled board entrypoint (src/task-board.js served HTML) → full test:all gate + dist rebuild (TASK-049). Design: add a chat panel to buildHtml() in src/task-board.js consuming the TASK-051 endpoints — establish a per-tab sessionId client-side matching SESSION_ID_RE (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, e.g. crypto.randomUUID with dashes kept), open EventSource('/api/chat/<id>/stream'), POST turns to /api/chat/<id>, render normalized {text|tool|subagent|turn-end|error} events incrementally. tool/subagent → distinct activity chips; error → inline error (no infinite spinner). XSS discipline = the existing board/graph pattern (createElement + textContent; innerHTML only for empty-clear). Regression locks follow the established scaffold-spec pattern for inline HTML (like the M3 /graph XSS pins in tests/knowledge-graph-scaffold.spec.js): grep the served chat HTML for the panel structure, EventSource usage, textContent/createElement (no innerHTML with stream content), and the activity-chip branch — NOT brittle DOM-render specs. UAT note: a true 'type → real orchestrator reply' run spawns a real claude child and spends the user's Agent-SDK credit; the orchestrator can verify the FULL wiring WITHOUT credit by injecting a fake bridge (the createBoardServer({bridge}) seam) emitting canned events and curling the SSE — the real-claude leg is a human live run (or rolls into TASK-056's live launch).

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body: APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOWUPS — 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 3 LOW / 1 NIT. All code ACs PASS, full test:all green 659 passed/5 skipped (incl dist-parity + existing board e2e 9/9 + chat-routes 15 + bridge 52 — no board regression). Traced: XSS clean (every event-text path text/tool/subagent/error goes through appendBubble()→createElement+textContent; the only innerHTML are two empty-string clears, identical to buildGraphHtml; no ${} interpolation of untrusted values) [AC4 PASS]. Incremental render correct (text event creates the assistant bubble on first delta, += appends on subsequent, turn-end finalizes so next turn = fresh bubble) [AC1 PASS]. Distinct chips: tool=amber 'chat-chip tool', subagent=blue 'chat-chip subagent', error='chat-chip error'+unblock; onerror→conn-lost chip+unblock — no infinite spinner [AC2/AC3 PASS]. Session id `'tab-'+crypto.randomUUID()` = 40 chars, [A-Za-z0-9-] only — matches SESSION_ID_RE so the server won't 400 turns [AC3 PASS]. 10 scaffold-grep locks non-vacuous + within the tests-after budget [AC5 PASS]. LOW: (1) SSE drop mid-stream orphans the partial bubble (no 'interrupted' marker — cosmetic, input still unblocks); (2) the Content-Type lock greps both tokens anywhere in the script region rather than co-occurring; (3) the fetch-POST lock greps `fetch(` not `method:'POST'` specifically. NIT: `sseConnected` assigned-but-never-read (dead var). All deferred to TASK-054 (revisits this UI). The live 'type→real reply' visual (AC6) is the orchestrator/human UAT leg, not in this diff.
